title: Union Eyes staging: remove fail-open legacy RLS policies from the deadline-engine tables
description: Mission UE-RUNTIME-REALITY-20261018 (Phase 3A). Business justification: the staging rls-verify preflight fails 1 of 1699 checks (manifest-rls deadline_reminder_executions UNENFORCED) and a runtime probe shows union_eyes_runtime with NO organization context can read, and insert into, deadline_reminders, deadline_audit_events and deadline_reminder_executions for every tenant. Cause: the PERMISSIVE PUBLIC policies installed by root migrations/0045 (deadline_reminders_tenant_isolation, deadline_audit_events_tenant_isolation, deadline_reminder_executions_read) fall back to the row's own organization when app.current_org_id is empty and are OR-ed with the 0010-style policies; the same objects exist in existing staging and in the clean-room/fresh path. Affected tables (exact scope): deadline_reminders, deadline_audit_events, deadline_reminder_executions. Desired state: RLS + FORCE + runtime and system policies and no PUBLIC policy on all three. Migration: canonical scoped migration apps/union-eyes/db/migrations-cache/0015_deadline_engine_rls_fail_closed_closure.sql (journal idx 15), executed only through the governed executor tooling/scripts/apply-union-eyes-scoped-migrations-existing-env.mjs (--check, then --apply). Atomic per migration with in-transaction post-condition assertions; idempotent; resumable; no grants, roles, functions or other tables. RELEASE ORDER (rehearsed; dossier 29_UE_PHASE3A_RUNTIME_REALITY_DOSSIER.md sections 14 and 18): CLOSURE FIRST, CANDIDATE SECOND. Apply 0015 BEFORE the candidate revision is dispatched and before it receives traffic; it does not depend on a newer revision serving. The serving revision (eae195f2, 0000259) cannot reach a policy-dependent statement on these tables on the live schema, and the candidate worker works under both policy sets. PREREQUISITES (all required before any staging apply): (1) approval by service_owner and change_manager; (2) the governed read-only ledger/catalog check recorded: ledger holds 0000-0005 under current hashes (otherwise STOP), rls-verify preflight fails only deadline_reminder_executions (1698/1699), legacy policies present; (3) stale 0%-traffic revisions 0000246-0000258 deactivated under a separate approved change so only the serving revision 0000259 (rollback target) and the candidate run; (4) maintainer security disposition covering the fail-open window until closure and the recovery policy (no executable fail-open restore); (5) COMMAND credential-containment disposition. NOT part of this change and independently blocking the candidate deploy: Django migrations content.0004 and grievances.0005 fail with DuplicateColumn on a lineage-restored database, and the schema prerequisites (deadline_reassignment_convergence, effective-due source fix). Not applied to staging at the time of writing.
impact_summary: Three deadline-engine tables, one governed migration, auto-rolled back on any failed statement or assertion. Behaviour change: sessions without tenant context stop seeing or writing these tables; the system role keeps full access via TO union_eyes_system policies. The serving revision is unaffected (rehearsed). With a staging-like ledger the governed --apply runs 0006-0015; on a staging-shaped database that changes exactly the three tables plus the ue_create_* helper function bodies.
rollback_plan: Recovery is forward and secure; the fail-closed state is never intentionally reverted, and there is no executable fail-open restore: a session variable or free-text token cannot evidence a real security decision, so none is accepted anywhere. Order of preference: (1) forward fix - deploy an application revision compatible with the closed policies; (2) approved point-in-time restore of nzila-staging-db (a change under its own approved record; restore rehearsed 2026-10-19, about 15 minutes); (3) if the closed state was altered by hand, replay 0015 directly in one transaction as the migration-admin principal (idempotent, ledger unchanged; the governed executor will not re-close because 0015 stays recorded) and re-run the rls-verify preflight. Traffic rollback is a weight change back to revision 0000259, which is compatible with the closed policies; once Django migrations have run, a weight flip alone may not be sufficient and recovery is (2). Any intentional reopening of cross-tenant access requires a NEW reviewed migration in a PR under a change record whose approved_by and approval_status are set by the actual approvers (service_owner, change_manager) with the maintainer security disposition attached; no agent or script may set them.
